candidates.claim: CORP_IN, bound to the corp interface, has an effective first entry permitting 192.168.30.102 to SCADA server 10.10.10.21 on tcp/502, which opens a direct CORP-to-OT connection that I1 forbids.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at fw-01:60 from CORP_IN unless it is separately approved and added to the registry.

candidates.claim: The effective CORP_IN permit at fw-01:60 carries CORP-to-OT traffic on tcp/502, a service that is not among the approved cross-zone services for the OT side.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at fw-01:60 from CORP_IN unless it is separately approved and added to the registry.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 EDGE_IN permits tcp/443 from any source to 203.0.113.2, the fw-01 outside address, while the ASA HTTP server is enabled, so HTTPS to the firewall is reachable from outside MGMT, which the management policy does not allow.
candidates.remediation: Remove the rtr-01 EDGE_IN permit for tcp/443 to 203.0.113.2 and confirm that the ASA HTTP server is limited to the MGMT source on the mgmt interface.

candidates.claim: The CORP_IN entry permitting 192.168.30.102 to 10.10.10.21 on tcp/502 is an addition that is not in the approved baseline.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile the added CORP_IN entry at fw-01:60 against the approved baseline and remove it unless it is approved.

clarifications.question: The registry defines OT-facing ports as sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/1-16, yet the approved trunks sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 ({10,99}), sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 ({10,99}) and sw-core-01 Gi1/0/24 ({10,20,30,99}) are active in VLAN 10. Should these uplink trunks be treated as OT-facing for the rule that only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, or is VLAN 10 on them a violation?
